parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain what is meant by gamma radiation ($\gamma$-radiation).

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem:
A source of gamma radiation is placed a fixed distance away from a detector and counter, as illustrated in Fig. 13.1.

{{figure:figure_13_1.png}}

A sheet of lead of thickness $x$ is placed between the source and the detector.

The average count rate $C$, corrected for background, is recorded. This is repeated for different values of $x$.

The variation with thickness $x$ of $\ln C$ is shown in Fig. 13.2.

{{figure:figure_13_2.png}}

The absorption of gamma radiation in lead may be represented by the equation

$$C=C_0\mathrm{e}^{-\mu x}$$

where $C_0$ is the count rate for $x=0$ and $\mu$ is the linear attenuation (absorption) coefficient.
parts.text:
Use Fig. 13.2 to determine the linear attenuation coefficient $\mu$ for this gamma radiation in lead.

μ (mm⁻¹)

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
The value of $\mu$ calculated in (b) is for gamma radiation in lead.

Suggest and explain whether the value of $\mu$ for aluminium would be the same, greater or smaller.
